title: Contingency Placement Agreements per Client and Line of Business
content:
**Rule.** A creditor client normally holds one agreement under the Contingency Placement Agreements, and may hold separate agreements only for genuinely separate lines of business — a health system's hospital and physician groups, or a utility's energy and telecom brands. A new agreement is issued only when the client holds no other agreement for the same line of business (the client industry recorded on the agreement) in pending signature, active, placement hold or runoff status, and a client holds at most 3 agreements that are not closed.

**Each agreement stands alone.** Each agreement carries its own tier, remittance terms, credit reporting authorization and balances. Nothing is pooled across a client's agreements except the volume used at tier review.

## Conditions for issuing a new agreement

Both conditions are read from the client's agreement records, matched on the same client and, for the first condition, the same line of business; the client's own account of what it holds is not the test.

| Condition | Met when |
|---|---|
| No open agreement for the same line of business | none of the client's agreements for that client industry is in pending signature, active, placement hold or runoff status |
| Agreement count | after the new agreement, the client holds no more than 3 agreements that are not closed |

A new agreement is issued only when both are met.

## Hypothetical cases

- A health system holds one active agreement for its hospital group and asks for a second agreement for its physician group, recorded as a separate client industry; it holds no other agreement. Neither condition is broken, and the new agreement may be issued.
- A utility holds an agreement for its energy brand in runoff and asks for a new agreement for the same energy brand. An agreement for the same line of business is still in runoff, so no new agreement is issued.
- A client holds three agreements for three different lines of business, none of them closed, and asks for a fourth line of business. A fourth agreement that is not closed would exceed 3, so no new agreement is issued.
- A client's earlier agreement for a line of business is closed. A closed agreement counts against neither condition.
